page: Vultr vcg-a40-2c-10g-4vram is a fractional GPU instance within the Cloud GPU family, designed to provide entry-level acceleration. The server features 2 shared vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel x86_64 core with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 10.0 GB of system memory, providing 5.0 GB per core. Graphics and parallel processing acceleration are delivered via a fractional slice (0.0833) of an NVIDIA Ampere A40 GPU, providing 4 GB of dedicated VRAM. Storage is supported by a local 180 GB NVMe SSD.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance split between CPU-bound tasks and GPU-accelerated workloads. The shared Intel CPU delivers average single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core scoring 1777.17 and single-threaded gzip compression reaching 25.28 GB/sec. However, multi-core CPU performance is weak, as indicated by a stress-ng multi-core score of 3494.92 and a PassMark CPU score of 3651.46. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with large-block read and write speeds falling into the bottom 25% tier. Database operations perform poorly, with PassMark database operations scoring 956.65.

Conversely, the fractional NVIDIA A40 GPU provides strong performance for specific machine learning tasks. LLM inference prompt processing speeds are strong, reaching 3480.67 tokens/sec for a small 135M model and 202.17 tokens/sec for a medium 7B model. Text generation on the 135M model is average at 114.49 tokens/sec. This hardware profile is highly cost-efficient for developers requiring GPU acceleration without the expense of a full dedicated GPU. It is best suited for light LLM inference, model prototyping, small-scale parallel processing, and basic GPU-accelerated development tasks, rather than heavy multi-threaded CPU computing or high-throughput database hosting.
